#1512. Fans fume at referee Andy Madley caught laughing and joking with Arsenal stars at half-time of win at Liverpool

Published: 06:03 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 07:58 EDT, 4 November 2026

Liverpool fans are fuming after referee Andy Madley laughed and joked with Arsenal's stars at half-time of their clash on Sunday – having denied them a penalty.

The Gunners claimed their first victory at Anfield since September 2012 thanks to Kai Havertz's goal, with the win sending Mikel Arteta's side three points clear of Manchester City.

But Reds supporters came away fuming after being denied a seeming stonewall penalty in the first half when Jurrien Timber tugged back Alexander Isak.

Isak had a golden chance to equalise when he rose to meet Bradley Barcola's cross, only to miss the ball after having his shirt pulled by Timber.

The Arsenal defender avoided punishment from Madley and VAR decided against intervening despite the vehement protests of Andoni Iraola and his players.

It was therefore extra galling for Liverpool fans to see the referee appearing to tell a joke to Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, and Declan Rice at half-time – though of course the encounter could have been entirely innocent.

Liverpool fans are fuming after referee Andy Madley was caught laughing and joking with Arsenal's players - having denied the Reds a penalty

Liverpool were denied a penalty after Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt

Fans claim Madley shouldn't have been cracking jokes with the Premier League champions

Part of refereeing, after all, is maintaining a relationship with players.

But for Liverpool it is another twist of the knife after a painful defeat which saw them fail to score from 18 shots and left them fifth in the Premier League.

'This referee clearly had a favourite. Liverpool got robbed in broad daylight,' one fan said on X.

'At any level of the game from Sunday pub league to Premier League, referees shouldn't be laughing and joking and high-fiving players on any side. They should turn up, ref neutrally, go home,' another said.

'He should not ref any more Arsenal games,' one added.

There is no evidence that Madley is biased towards the Premier League champions.

Sky Sports pundits Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright unanimously agreed Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty at half-time and suggested that Isak was denied the spot-kick because he failed to make more of the incident.

Iraola thinks the game could have gone differently had Madley not missed Timber's shirt pull.

The Liverpool boss said after the match: ‘There are two situations and they are a little bit related. The Isak one is a clear penalty.

‘He's gonna head the ball in front of the goal, and they grab him where everyone sees the shirt. You don't need a lot, just to avoid Alex, because the ball just goes in front of him, and I don't see the reason why, probably because he doesn't dive or he doesn't go to the floor. It shouldn't be a reason not to concede a penalty.'

Liverpool were irate as they lost to Arsenal at home for the first time since September 2012

Iraola also pointed to a similar situation where Cody Gakpo was tugged back, but the officials said the Dutchman would not get to the ball.

‘They say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn't have arrived to the ball, but then you're basically accepting that the first one is, is a pen, no?’ added Iraola. ‘So you cannot use the argument in both ways differently. So I think it's a, yes, it's a pen, the Alex one is.’

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, the manager said: 'It's a problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor. The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

'It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it.'

Asked if he will tell Isak to do that in future, the Spaniard replied: 'Yes, definitely.'

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk took aim at VAR too after the match, expressing his disappointment at the defeat.

'I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back and I've seen it being given. Today it wasn't meant to be,' he said.

Asked if Isak should have reacted more, the Dutchman added: 'We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras?

'Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal.'

Former Liverpool defender Carragher was furious that VAR had not intervened as he analysed the incident at half-time.

'One of the best goal-scorers in the league is pulled back seven yards from goal, and the pull back stops him heading the ball. Why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job,' he said bluntly.

Arsenal moved to the top of the table on 24 points with victory at Anfield, while Liverpool remained fifth after Brighton and Chelsea, who are third and fourth respectively, both won on Saturday.

Mikel Arteta hailed his side’s resilience to win at Anfield.

Asked if it feels better to do so as a player or manager, he said: ‘Now it feels better as a manager, it has been such a long time without this feeling. We are extremely proud, especially the conditions we arrived in after the defeat against Fleetwood looked like the end of the world.

‘But then you have to pick yourself up. Four days later you have to come to Anfield against this manager and this team.’

#1511. GdS: A fourth failed test – Amorim risks going off track with consistent rotations

After another poor performance in midweek, questions are being asked about Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan squad and his ability to rotate.

Amorim isn’t exactly to blame for last night; after a busy October, he had to rotate. However, results aren’t as strong when he opts to remove the starters and last night’s defeat to Ferencvaros is only the latest example of this issue.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gazzetta dello Sport writes that the Rossoneri are a team that loses its bearings whenever a rotation occurs. Indeed, even a few months in, Amorim can only trust a few of his players to work in his system.

The Derby della Madonnina should’ve fueled the squad, but a rotated squad lacked intensity and showed no signs of desire to build some momentum. Indeed, the gap between the starters and the reserves was stark, too stark.

Across the pitch, performances were poor – as the fan ratings showed – and age cannot be an excuse. After all, they were not hung out to dry against a European elite, it was a winnable game.

This fourth test, as Gazzetta puts it, was a failure and it’s now the third time that they’ve fallen in Europe. Even against Bologna, with slight rotations, they fell. So, Amorim may now be reluctant to rotate as heavily, but that brings up new issues. If they keep going at this rate, they’ll head off track.

#1510. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1509. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1508. French team: Zinédine Zidane’s list still promises something new

At 6 p.m., Zinédine Zidane will reveal the list of players selected to play the last two Nations League matches against Italy (November 12) and Turkey (November 15). A list in which several injured players will not appear, such as Ousmane Dembélé, Jules Koundé, Estéban Lepaul, William Saliba or even Maxence Lacroix. On the other hand, several returns are expected, starting with that of the captain, Kylian Mbappé. Called up in September, the Real Madrid striker left his partners just after the first match in Türkiye due to a knee injury. Since then, the “Kyks” are thriving again (8 goals in 7 matches) and will be very present.

Ditto for his partners at Casa Blanca, Ibrahima Konaté and Aurélien Tchouameni, as well as for the Parisian Warren Zaire-Emery, also deprived of the first gathering due to an injury. Titi could even become a solution at right-back again, even if Zidane had declared that he had summoned him to play in the middle. All this would therefore be at the expense of Malo Gusto lacking playing time at Chelsea. With the packages of Koundé, Lacroix and Saliba, the defensive sector will therefore inevitably open the door to a few new players.

Called up for the first time by Zidane in September, Jérémy Jacquet and Leny Yoro, as well as Pierre Kalulu and Adrien Truffert (already summoned by Deschamps), will still be there, but The Team announces that Lucas Hernandez and Castello Lukeba could have a card to play in the axis. Yesterday, we also revealed to you that Sunderland left-back, Dayann Méthalie, received a pre-call-up. Ditto for Al-Ahli midfielder Valentin Atangana. For the goalkeeper position, Mike Maignan, Guillaume Restes and Jean Butez should be reappointed. Robin Risser remains an option, but The Team assures that Fabien Barthez really appreciated the last gathering of his doormen.

Finally, in terms of attack, Zinédine Zidane faces a headache. With the absence of Lepaul, the natural solution Marcus Thuram exists, but the Interist is far from unanimous internally, with some expressing doubts about his ability to integrate into the new ZZ project. The Tottenham player Mathys Tel has supporters within the French staff, but the novelty could be the choice to develop the versatile Maghnes Akliouche in the axis, alongside Mbappé. The former Monegasque is one of the players most used by Luis Enrique at PSG and he is seriously starting to put together a series of convincing performances. Eli Junior Kroupi remains an option, but the Bournemouth striker is only just returning from injury.

#1507. New footage shows how goalkeeper in Spanish footballer's killer collision was fired-up in moments before 'reckless' tackle - as police probe medical team after opening homicide investigation

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and NATALIA PENZA

Published: 05:13 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:28 EDT, 4 November 2026

New footage has revealed the tense moments before goalkeeper Jesus Owono launched a 'reckless' tackle that led to the death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker De Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

A homicide squad has launched an investigation as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation, with police now also probing the medical response to the incident.

Now, new footage taken from the stands has revealed how a fired-up Owono behaved in the moments leading up to the devastating collision.

The video shows how Owono had made his way to the other end of the pitch to get involved in a confrontation following a red card for opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, before appearing to motion for him to make his way off the field of play.

Footage has revealed the heated build-up to the tackle that led to the death of Jesus de Miguel, which showed goalkeeper Jesus Owono arguing with his rival goalkeeper. (Source: X/Eldense_)

Fans have commented in Owono's involvement in an argument with opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, who was sent off in the closing stages of the match (Source: X/Eldense_)

Martin and Owono appeared to continue their argument as they exchanged gestures as the Tenerife shot-stopper departed the scene.

The footage then captured Owono's wild celebrations - in which he leapt into the air and punched his fist - as Andorra FC scored an 88th minute equaliser.

'Here you have the images prior to the action by goalkeeper Owono, in the parts where he's not in focus — in one of them, he's confronting and saying things to the rival goalkeeper, and in the other, celebrating the goal right in the face of the Tenerife stands,' one fan wrote.

'He's a repeat offender when it comes to this kind of behavior.'

Another said: 'There isn't anyone from those of us who were in the stadium who didn't agree with the opinion that the entry was reckless. That it was an assault. It's clear that he didn't want the final outcome, but it's also clear that it wasn't an isolated incident.'

'I'm right behind that goal! Owono was completely unhinged! He came all the way to the rival goal to confront Dani, the Tenerife goalkeeper, over Lautaro's red card, and started gesticulating wildly at Dani to get him off the field after being sent off! This guy was totally out of his mind,' a third posted.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

De Miguel died on Tuesday morning following a horrifying clash with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

Andorra FC defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected’ by the tragedy.

‘There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,’ Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

‘What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

‘First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch,' he said.

‘I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

‘In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether Jesus de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died yesterday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his second-division club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Police investigating the death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel are probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono

Well-placed sources told local press overnight there were 'certain discrepancies within the reports, or potential inaccuracies when compared to other evidence in the case' such as video footage recorded and posted on social media.

Respected island newspaper El Dia said: 'Among the issues currently under investigation, which according to sources remained unresolved as of yesterday, is whether the medical team who rushed from the sidelines to the centre of the pitch carrying a stretcher, a spinal board, and an Automated External Defibrillator to attend to the player, acted with due diligence during the more than six minutes they spent on the pitch before placing him on the spinal board for transport to an ambulance, which was stationed at one of the stadium access gates on La Mutine Street.'

It added: 'Investigators are also looking into an even more striking question.

'After a Guedel airway, a curved, semi-rigid oropharyngeal tube, was inserted into the player's mouth following his loss of consciousness, to prevent his tongue from obstructing his airway, was he also provided with oxygen during the resuscitation efforts on the pitch, as is required by protocol?

'According to sources, efforts are still underway to gather all available evidence to determine whether De Miguel was administered oxygen, either via a bag-valve mask (Ambu bag) or a face mask connected to one of the oxygen cylinders kept pitchside at the stadium.

'Sources indicate that this remains unresolved, at least regarding the medical care provided on the field of play.

'Furthermore, footage of the player being transported on a spinal board suggests that oxygen was not being administered during that process.

'Additionally, during the evacuation from the centre of the pitch to the ambulance, the player was carried on a spinal board by individuals who were moving at a jog.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel outside the entrance to Tenerife's stadium

'The manner in which the patient was transported, which should never have been carried out in such a way, was highly dangerous to their physical well-being.'

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who has lived in Spain since he was eight, was red-carded for kneeing Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel in the chest near the halfway line late into stoppage time. The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Maria and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time yesterday morning he had died at a hospital in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz about 8am, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats'.

It said in a statement, after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened: 'Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, which occurred this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8am.

'There are no words of comfort, there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow.

'We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire 'tinerfeñismo' community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Owono is reportedly intending to apologise directly to de Miguel's family for his challenge and has made his social media private following abusive chants and messages he received (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Owono is reportedly seeking to apologise to Jesus de Miguel's family before making any kind of public statement.

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said yesterday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

Later today Jesus de Miguel's body is expected to be flown to the Spanish mainland so his funeral can take place in the town where his parents hail from.

The 30-year-old footballer's mum and dad travelled to Tenerife after being told about the severity of his injuries before confirmation this morning he had died in an island hospital.

They will now make the reverse trip to Madrid before travelling to Navahermosa in the province of Toledo 80 miles south-west of the Spanish capital which they have chosen as the place for the player's funeral.

Jesus's club revealed the location yesterday afternoon but said it was unable to say at this stage when exactly it would be.

Town hall officials in Navahermosa, which has a population of just over 3,500 inhabitants, said immediately after learning of the footballer's death: 'Since yesterday, we had held onto the hope that Jesus might overcome the toughest match of his life. However, we woke up today to the worst possible news.

'On behalf of the town hall, we wish to express our deepest sorrow at this tragic outcome. We want to extend all our love, support, and affection to his family, friends, and everyone who is feeling this loss today.

'There are no words that can ease such profound pain, but please know that we are by your side and that we share in your sadness.

'Jesus, you have always been, and will always remain, a source of pride for us.

'Today, with broken hearts, we must say goodbye, but we will hold onto your memory. Rest in peace.'

Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region which includes Navahermosa and the province of Toledo where a train crash last Wednesday claimed the lives of 69 people, added in his own statement: 'I am at a loss for words; the passing of footballer Jesus de Miguel, while doing what he loved most and what he had fought so hard for, playing football, is heartbreaking news.

'My thoughts are with his family, who hail from the municipality of Navahermosa in the province of Toledo. My deepest condolences.'

The entire CD Tenerife squad will travel to Navahermosa to pay their last respects to their teammate.

Flags outside the town hall flew at half mast today.

The National Police in the island capital Santa Cruz has yet to release an official statement about its ongoing probe.

A minute's silence was held before Champions League matches in memory of De Miguel on Tuesday

But a force spokesman said yesterday evening: 'An investigation is underway into the circumstances surrounding the incident which led to Jesus de Miguel's death which is being conducted by the homicide unit.

'It has been opened because the death was not the result of natural causes and it will seek to determine whether in terms of the law, an involuntary manslaughter could have been committed.'

The report police draft as a result of their probe will be submitted to a local judge whose job it will be to decide whether to take the matter further.

A Canary Islands court source described the collision between the two footballers as 'an accidental collision on the playing field.'

But he added: 'Any death not resulting from natural causes, referred to as a 'forensic death,' whether due to an accident or other factors, automatically triggers a judicial investigation, which is the case here.'

Court officials said this morning they weren't able to comment on when they expected to receive the police report into the drama.

One said: 'At the moment the investigation is still in the hands of police who will submit their report to a court in Santa Cruz once officers have completed their work.'

#1506. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Five things we learned – a poor squad picked apart

AC Milan’s Europa League misery continued at San Siro on Thursday night as they were beaten 2-0 by Ferencvaros.

Ruben Amorim made six changes to the team that won the derby against Inter, hoping that the entire group would remain buoyed by that performance to secure a much-needed win in Europe. However, what followed was the worst performance of his tenure so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Lenny Joseph netted twice in the second half to capitalise on errors and fire the Hungarian side to a memorable win. Ferencvaros were not even rocked by a red card to the substitute Yusuf as they kept the Rossoneri at bay quite easily, securing a two-goal win they deserved.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from another dismal midweek game.

It’s difficult to pick five talking points after a game like this, as we can probably spend quite a bit of time discussing how bad each of the players were. But let’s try to address the bigger issue.

This squad is full of sheep, lacking both leaders and the quality to compete. We can talk all about how much Amorim rotates the squad and try to ease the blow by suggesting the Rossoneri didn’t field their best XI. Yet, if the management were serious about making the club competitive, then the rotational players should be above the quality of almost all teams competing in the Europa League, bar a few.

Obviously, if we assume Amorim is the right choice and Gerry Cardinale is serious, then it will take a lot more than a single transfer window and three new players to get Milan to compete on a few fronts, which was further proven against Ferencvaros.

Out of the whole squad, the only player that can change a game is Diego Moreira, who doesn’t play every game and has lots of room for improvement still. Not to mention that playing with the likes of Filippo Terracciano, Ardon Jashari and even Goncalo Ramos is not helping Belgium at all.

The rest of the squad lack either the quality or the mentality. The collective arrogance on the pitch was insufferable to watch, with Ferencvaros looking like the only side that had any desire to actually win. Whilst the Diavolo looked like they were playing a game in the park with no aggression, no focus, no intensity. No nothing.

It’s a bit pointless to discuss individuals because I think the wider point is clear – Milan lack leaders, Milan lack quality and Milan lack a game changer that can get the ball and make something happen when the tough gets going.

It was made evident after four games in the Europa League and a few blunders in Serie A that there’s lots of work to be done in January and next summer.

Again, it’s difficult to pick and choose which player to discuss, but given Ramos is the Rossoneri’s most expensive signing ever, it’s probably fair that the pressure starts mounting on him.

Listen, I wasn’t too bothered by the lack of goals initially, as the striker did well in the build-up and opened up space for his teammates; he also ran a lot in both phases of the game. Let’s also be honest, he has lacked the service to actually get the goal-scoring opportunities.

Nevertheless, in the last few games and especially against Ferencvaros, he has been dire – his build-up is poor, his ball control is pretty bad and when he does get a shot off, it’s usually miles away.

Now, obviously he’s not a striker that’s going to create chances for himself; he lacks the pace and the trickery, which is fine if you are good in the other aspects of the game. However, we can’t keep grasping for straws.

The reality is that the former PSG man is just not living up to the expectations given the hefty sum paid for him in the summer.

In retrospect, maybe it wasn’t wise to spend such a sum on a player who needs quality around him in order to be a better facilitator or to receive more chances overall. The reality as of now is that the Portuguese is a disappointment.

Again, as we said, most players in the squad lack quality or mentality and unfortunately for us there are some that lack both and it’s way past the tipping point at this stage.

Terracciano, for starters, has not shown anything worth mentioning in all of his games with the red and black shirt and there’s really no reason for him to get minutes. Even without pressure, he’s just not of the needed level.

Jashari is another one that the fans and the management have hoped will bounce back after his lengthy injury after joining Milan. Yet, he’s probably had one good game from start to finish and there’s always gaps in his game.

It’s probably wise at this point to accept he’s not going to live up to the expectations and a solution needs to be found on the market, especially given Luka Modric will most likely be retiring at the end of the season.

There are also other players in this category that didn’t necessarily participate in last night’s game but should have the same fate – Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek to name a couple.

If nothing else, these poor performances should highlight to the management where the gap in quality is and what the strategy on the transfer market should be.

4. De Winter’s disastrous performance proves costly

I think the biggest individual call-out should definitely be the Belgian, who played an awful back pass to Lorenzo Torriani on the first goal. Yes, the keeper could’ve and should’ve done much better, but that back pass was just so sloppy – it could put an outfield player in a tricky situation, let alone a goalkeeper that perhaps isn’t as comfortable with his feet.

This especially coming from a player who should’ve been a certainty at the back given the heavily rotated squad.

We can also partly criticise the intervention on the second goal, because it started the whole sequence leading to the Joseph’s brace. Yes, it was a bit unlucky where the ball ended up, but you can also argue it was sloppy, the same way you can argue that a keeper clearing the ball into the opponent’s feet after a shot instead of towards the corner is the keeper’s fault to an extent.

It’s just unacceptable to go from bullying Thuram to being bullied by not even Ferencvaros’s first-choice striker.

5. Amorim’s tactics fail, but the players also struggle

I think it’s probably fair to criticise the Portuguese coach a bit too, as the Hungarians totally outplayed the Diavolo at the San Siro and were tactically better. All in all, they had the answer to everything Milan tried to offer on the night.

At the same time, I’m torn to put the blame fully on Ruben Amorim because he did make a triple change at half-time, bringing on Pulisic, Moreira and Gila, which was still at 0-0. At that point, the Rossoneri had more than enough quality on the pitch to be able to deal with whatever Ferencvaros had to offer.

Instead, two individual mistakes gave away the opening goal and it all went downhill from there. Even after the red card, Milan struggled to create a big chance.

I personally struggle to blame this fully on tactics given all the circumstances and we are back to the point that the Milan squad are just not good enough and lacks that killer mentality.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Spot on. Ultimately blame needs to be laid at the door of the players. A coach can only do so much, all these schoolboy errors are indefensible.

Agreed. This is totally on the players. I can forgive the first half as the starters at least kept it 0-0 through halftime despite being outgunned talent-wise given Milan’s weak bench. But the 2nd half was pitiful – our best players were on and other than the first 5-7 minutes of the half, we were toothless. Little energy or fire displayed.

Even when they are not playing, find a way to mention Estupinian and RLC. 16 players played like A6S, none of them named Estupinian or RLC, 10 of them weren’t mentioned at all in the whole article, but 2 players that didn’t play were specifically mentioned. From this game we learned that Estupinian and RLC are not so bad when compared to Bartesaghi, Terracciano, Musah, Jashari.

We learned that Anorim doesn’t understands players positions and has no idea what he is doing at this stage. Every game is a new formation, with new positions for half of the team. You can’t have any chemistry that way. Just look at Rabiot in the end destroying a great chance for Camarda while Rabiot was offside. That’s what happens when you play a mid as a striker out of nowhere. Or on the other side playing AM/SS player like Cisse as a Left mid while the guy is super slow so he can’t cover anything in the mid… Its all on the coach. A Hungarian team definitely does not have better players than Milan, but they have a coach who understands basic players positions and they also had team chemistry from constantly playing in the same formation/roles.

Spot on,but Amorin has no fault,the blame should go to whoever’s decision it was to hire him.

What is the identity of this team? We have a coach who has been known for his 343 or 3421 system and all of a sudden he is playing 442 or 4411. Was the change forced by the injuries or else? For what system are they going to look for reinforcements in January?

Regardless of what I think of Ramos and his transfer, it’s difficult for any striker to contribute when your defenders and midfielders can’t get the ball in the opposing team part of the pitch. Milan had over 60% possession in the 1st half and all of it was in their own half of the pitch. The 4 defenders, the 3 midfielders plus Cisse were embarrassing in the 1st half. Don’t let the score fool you, the 1st half was much worse than the 2nd.

We have a similar situation as when Fonseca was here. You hire a coach because you want to play attacking possession style football but you don’t have the players for it. Milan midfielders can’t receive the ball cleanly, can’t hold on to the ball, can’t make the simplest of passes. Jashari is so bad it got me wishing Ricci was playing instead. Thats how bad he is. From what I’ve seen in his serie A career I would rather have Bondo playing instead of Jashari, but for some reason he is excluded from the squad. Play Comotto!!!

Krösche needs to get to work immediately. Clean up the trash and sign actual footballers, not some dudes who only do cardio with bricks for feet and sh!t for brains.

“You hire a coach because you want to play attacking possession style football but you don’t have the players for it.” Didn’t Amorim say after the summer that he is satisfied of the transfer ? Didn’t he approve of many of the transfers ? Didn’t he veto the depature of some players like Estupiñán and RLC while sending Nkunku and Fofana away ? Also Amorim and “attacking” football ? Did you watch some of his games with Manchester United ? He was basically Allegri 2.0

Oh we CAN definitely still put blame on the coach. Look at this lineup and tell me it inspired confidence…

I just don’t understand. We basically have close to a best starting XI. Maignon, Gila, De Winter, Pav, Modric, Rabiot, Moreira, (bad left wing back) Pulisic, Cisse , and Ramos. Every game you have one or two of these players sit and get a rest. And maybe for the derbies you play your best XI. That’s rotation. This idea of replacing 5-6 players at once is a recipe for disaster, there is a reason no one does this. Plus for the love of God Ramos and Rabiot every game for 90? Why? They are worn out.

It seems like Amorim has decided that the EL is less important than serie A and, because of the lack of depth, use the bench players for games. And it seems, because of that, the players themselves decided to treat the EL as an inconvenience rather than a tournament to play, which is undefensible. I say this, it’s because, aside from the bench players (Terracciano, Bartesaghi,..) our regulars were also bad and seemed disinterested and the subs didn’t add a lot and seemed far from what they’ve shown in the derby. You can’t blame the coach if our players can’t even win 50/50 against Ferencváros’ players. As for the coach, he doesn’t get to complain about us not having the team to compete on 2 fronts, when he asked for the departure of many players, some of whom better than some regulars and he doesn’t get to complain where has like a new system every other game.

I said it before the season started. This will be a transition year. Too much damage was done by the Cardinale and the previous management to be fixed in a season. Are Cardinale and Amorim the guys to bring Milan back? I don’t think so, but that will be clearer in January/February. Let’s focus on the positives for the time being: 1. Despite not playing well, results in Serie A have been decent. It feels very similar to last season (hopefully ends differently). 2. With Inter playing Como this weekend, we can close the gap on one or both of them by beating Genoa 3. Juventus, Napoli, and Atalanta still haven’t found their footing 4. Despite the horrible start to the Europa League, the joke of a new format really helps us. 24 teams qualify. Winning two of the remaining four games gives us over 50% chance of qualifying. Two wins and a draw pretty much guarantees it.
